headline: Sox Bats Fall Silent In Depressing Six To One Loss At Fenway
morning_brew: That was an absolutely brutal night at Fenway Park. We drop a six to one dud to Toronto, and my head is spinning. Payton Tolle actually battled through five innings, but you can't win baseball games when your lineup decides to take the night off. We scraped together eight hits but only managed a single run. I watched us leave runner after runner on base, and it felt like watching rush hour traffic crawl on the Pike.

Ceddanne Rafaela had a decent night with two hits, but the rest of the bats were completely asleep. Willson Contreras went zero for four and Wilyer Abreu went zero for three, which is just not going to cut it. My old man always said that hits are like city buses, because you wait forever for one and then three show up at once, but last night the bus never even left the station. Then Ryan Watson comes out and serves up two more runs in the ninth to put the game completely out of reach. It's just depressing.

Down in Foxborough, the Patriots are in the news for suing the town over nearly a million dollars in entertainment license fees. Robert Kraft is fighting over security costs at Gillette, which is a classic offseason distraction when we should be focusing on Drake Maye and mandatory minicamp. Still, I'd rather talk about stadium licensing gripes than watch this baseball team lose another series opener. We need a bounce-back tonight or this season is going down the drain.
